messages:
nina: Quick RFC follow-up: deciding multiplexed regional front-door vs per-tenant proxies for private endpoints. multiplexing saves ENIs/IPs but raises SNI/auth and src-ip preservation issues. looking for ops and rollback thoughts.

raj: ENI quotas are our blocker. multiplex for self-serve makes infra much cheaper. we should prototype. :+1:

lucy: Isolation is the big risk. need tenant-level circuit breakers and per-tenant QoS before enabling multiplexing for many customers.

nina: TLS modes we considered: passthrough (SNI->tenant), terminate (relay handles certs), hybrid (enterprise passthrough, hosted terminate). each has tradeoffs for telemetry and cert ownership.

paul: For source-IP allowlists, only dedicated ENI or pinning preserves true srcip. otherwise we must send signed x-forwarded-for header. ops/legal will ask.

raj: Rollback requirement: fast pin-to-dedicated-proxy and an emergency isolate API to cut a tenant out of multiplex pool. otherwise cutovers are risky.

ops-bot: CI: multiplex-spike passed smoke tests (image: rwd/multiplex-spike:canary).

nina: Action items: isolation spike (simulate noisy tenant) -> raj + lucy (due next Fri). ops/backout runbook -> paul (draft Wed). i'll draft SNI cache and perf budget.

lucy: Guardrails before broad rollout: per-tenant quotas, tokenized trace headers, circuit breakers, and instant kill-switch.

nina: ok will capture in RFC follow-up. any objections to hybrid as enterprise default? speak now.
